newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares better supported after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: German shares better supported after U.S. data.

text.p: German shares were seen better supported within an albeit tight range after U.S. jobless and payrolls data reversed some of the institutional short-selling that had been weighing on market prices.

The IBIS DAX index of all-day computer trading wiped out earlier losses to stand almost flat at 2,534.33 points by 1426 GMT Friday compared to a day-low of 2,515.18. The DAX bourse index had earlier closed 12.54 points down at 2,517.0.
"We've been seeing some short-selling that people are now deciding to cover," one trader said, adding that he believed the selling had been overdone.
September DAX futures stood 4.0 points higher at 2,539 points, up from a day-low of 2,516.0.

Dealers said that while the U.S. payroll figures, which showed a slightly higher than expected gain of 250,000 in August, were fundamentally negative for German shares in that they carried a risk of higher U.S. interest rates, the market impact was limited.
"As earlier this week, when German GDP figures showed growth in the economy, it seems that the significance was already largely priced into the market," one said.
The dollar's strength provided further support.
The U.S. currency traded at around 1.4886/91 to the mark around 1449 GMT compared to a level of around 1.4857/67 before the U.S. figures.
But a number of traders said that despite the positive influences German shares were now likely to trade in a tight range because of an expected lack of corporate news.
"I see a trading range of between 2,500 and 2,550 in the short-term," one said.
